title: General Cluster Experiment Estimators under Network Interference
text: function returns list , supplied data, causal_effects — overall (CE^O), direct (CE^D(phi_1), CE^D(phi_0)), indirect (CE^(1), CE^(0)) total (CE^T) effects, estimate, variance standard error. Effects well-defined given regimes returned NA well_defined = FALSE. potential_outcomes — well-defined marginal Ybar(phi) non-marginal Ybar(w, phi) population average potential outcomes, variances. title: General Cluster Experiment Estimators under Network Interference
text: See ?mrn, ?iptw ?crn full documentation examples.
code: library(generalClusterExp)  ## Small geometric cluster network: units live around ten cluster centres ## and interfere with all units within distance 1.5. set.seed(1) n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per)                      # cluster ids centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4   # cluster centres loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2) # unit locations A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1  ## Two-stage assignment: clusters are treated w.p. 0.7; units in treated ## clusters get W = 1 w.p. 0.5 (regime phi_1), units in control clusters ## w.p. 0.2 (regime phi_0). W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7) W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))  ## Outcomes with neighbourhood interference. Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +                  W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))  fit <- mrn(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,            dist1 = "binom", params1 = list(prob = 0.5),            dist0 = "binom", params0 = list(prob = 0.2),            distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7)) fit$causal_effects fit$potential_outcomes  ## Cluster-level complete randomization (exactly 7 of 10 clusters treated) ## automatically switches to the bias-corrected variance estimator: W_C2 <- as.integer(seq_len(K) %in% sample.int(K, 7)) W_Y2 <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C2[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2)) Y2 <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y2) +                   W_Y2 * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y2)) + rnorm(n)) fit_bc <- mrn(A, C, Y2, W_C2, W_Y2,               params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),               distC = "hypergeom", paramsC = list(m = 7)) fit_bc$variance_type

title: General Cluster Experiment Estimators under Network Interference
text: section, theorem proposition numbers refer arXiv:2607.04644. Estimands — direct, indirect, total overall causal effects, marginal / non-marginal population average potential outcomes: Section 3 (“Setup identification”). complete Radon–Nikodym → crn(), (iv) cluster-level IPTW → iptw(). Estimators — Hájek linear-weighted estimators weight matrices B, B_marg: Section 4. Variance estimators — Section 5. Theorem 5.4 gives Sigma1, Löwner maximum within-cluster (K1) cross-cluster (K2) HAC kernels independent Bernoulli randomization. Theorem 5.9 gives Sigma2, cluster-agnostic estimator built K3+. Theorem 5.11(ii) gives Sigma3 = Sigma1 - M, bias-corrected estimator cluster-level complete randomization. crn() uses Sigma2 every design. Theorem 5.9 establishes conservativeness independent Bernoulli randomization; paper extend Sigma2 complete randomization, design reported crn() variance read heuristic.

title: CRN estimator (complete Radon–Nikodym weights) — crn
text: Cluster-agnostic linear-weighted Hajek estimator using complete (joint) Radon–Nikodym identification weights (Theorem 3.7, Proposition 3.9(ii)). outputs mrn. variance estimator cluster-agnostic HAC estimator \(\hat\Sigma_2\) built PSD part \(K_3^+\) interference kernel, used every value design. conservativeness established Theorem 5.9 independent Bernoulli randomization; companion manuscript cover \(\hat\Sigma_2\) complete randomization, treat variance heuristic case.

title: CRN estimator (complete Radon–Nikodym weights) — crn
code: crn(   A,   C,   Y,   W_C,   W_Y,   dist1 = "binom",   params1 = list(prob = 0.5),   dist0 = "binom",   params0 = list(prob = 0),   distC = "binom",   paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),   unit_weights = NULL,   design = NULL )

title: CRN estimator (complete Radon–Nikodym weights) — crn
text: n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix interference network (self-loops, used throughout project). C integer vector length n_unit giving unit's cluster id. Y numeric vector observed outcomes (length n_unit). W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments, indexed cluster id. W_Y 0/1 vector individual-level treatments (length n_unit). dist1, params1 within-cluster assignment law treated regime phi_1. dist0, params0 within-cluster assignment law control regime phi_0. distC, paramsC cluster-level assignment law. unit_weights optional per-unit weights u_i = g_i / N_i (default: uniform 1 / n_unit). design optional override, "bernoulli" "complete"; inferred distC NULL.

title: CRN estimator (complete Radon–Nikodym weights) — crn
text: See mrn.

title: CRN estimator (complete Radon–Nikodym weights) — crn
code: ## Same data-generating pipeline as in the mrn() example: geometric ## cluster network, two-stage Bernoulli treatment, interference outcomes. set.seed(1) n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per) centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4 loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2) A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1  W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7) W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2)) Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +                  W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))  ## CRN is cluster-agnostic: its variance uses the PSD-projected ## interference kernel K3+ (Sigma2, Theorem 5.9). fit <- crn(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,            params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),            distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7)) fit$variance_type #> [1] "var_2 (K3+)" fit$causal_effects #>                       effect            key estimate  variance        se #> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 4.837794 1.1419603 1.0686254 #> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 4.669199 1.2697475 1.1268307 #> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 3.924290 0.3952255 0.6286696 #> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 3.947648 1.2956863 1.1382822 #> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 3.202740 0.2320907 0.4817579 #> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 7.871939 1.7474932 1.3219279 #>   well_defined #> 1         TRUE #> 2         TRUE #> 3         TRUE #> 4         TRUE #> 5         TRUE #> 6         TRUE

what: Assemble the HAC covariance for a (method, design) pair — .assemble_Sigma
title: Assemble the HAC covariance for a (method, design) pair — .assemble_Sigma
text: Assembles d x d HAC covariance supplied contribution matrix V, following variance rule (method, design) pair: crn: \(\hat\Sigma_2 = V^\top K_3^+ V\) (Theorem 5.9); mrn / iptw, Bernoulli:     \(\hat\Sigma_1 = \hat\Sigma^{K_1} \vee \hat\Sigma^{K_2}\), Loewner     max within- overlap-kernel covariances (Theorem 5.4); mrn / iptw, complete:     \(\hat\Sigma_3 = \hat\Sigma_1 - \hat M\) (Theorem 5.11(ii)).

code: .assemble_Sigma(V, A, C, W_C, method, design)

title: Assemble the HAC covariance for a (method, design) pair — .assemble_Sigma
text: V n_unit x d contribution matrix. n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix (self-loops). C integer vector cluster ids. W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments. method "mrn", "iptw" "crn". design "bernoulli" "complete".

title: Assemble the HAC covariance for a (method, design) pair — .assemble_Sigma
code: set.seed(1) A <- Matrix::Matrix(outer(1:12, 1:12, function(i, j) abs(i - j) <= 1) * 1,                     sparse = TRUE) C <- rep(1:3, each = 4); W_C <- c(1, 0, 1) V <- matrix(rnorm(24), 12, 2) / 12   # contributions of two estimands generalClusterExp:::.assemble_Sigma(V, A, C, W_C,                                     method = "mrn", design = "bernoulli") #> $Sigma #>            [,1]       [,2] #> [1,] 0.08862573 0.04373699 #> [2,] 0.04373699 0.08922703 #>  #> $variance_type #> [1] "var_1 (Loewner-max, Bernoulli)" #>  generalClusterExp:::.assemble_Sigma(V, A, C, W_C,                                     method = "crn", design = "bernoulli") #> $Sigma #>            [,1]       [,2] #> [1,] 0.09709699 0.03503498 #> [2,] 0.03503498 0.21256676 #>  #> $variance_type #> [1] "var_2 (K3+)" #>

title: Bias-correction matrix under complete randomization — .bias_correction_matrix
text: Bias-correction matrix \(\hat M\) cluster-level (stratified) complete randomization (Section 5.2; bias-corrected estimator \(\hat\Sigma_3 = \hat\Sigma_1 - \hat M\) Theorem 5.11(ii)): $$\hat M = \sum_{k : p_k \(p_{overlap}, 1 - p_{overlap})}       \hat s_k \hat s_k^\top / (|I_k| p_k (1 - p_k)),$$ $$\hat s_k = \sum_{(,j)} (T_{ij,k} - m_{ij,k} p_k) V_{ij},$$ \(T_{ij,k}\) number treated clusters stratum k \(N^{cl}_{ij}\), \(m_{ij,k}\) number clusters stratum k \(N^{cl}_{ij}\), \(p_k\) realised treated fraction stratum k.

title: Bias-correction matrix under complete randomization — .bias_correction_matrix
code: .bias_correction_matrix(A, C, W_C, V, strata = NULL, p_overlap = 0)

title: Bias-correction matrix under complete randomization — .bias_correction_matrix
text: n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix (self-loops). C integer vector cluster ids. W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments, indexed cluster id. V n_unit x d contribution matrix. strata list cluster-id vectors; NULL means one stratum. p_overlap strata \(p_k\) outside \((p_{overlap}, 1 - p_{overlap})\) skipped.

Complete / joint Radon–Nikodym (CRN) identification weights — .complete_rn_weights
text: Per-unit complete (joint) Radon–Nikodym weights \(\alpha_{ij}^{comp}\) (Theorem 3.7, Proposition 3.9(ii)); cluster-agnostic. Unlike marginal weights, condition realised cluster-level assignment, taking product per-cluster likelihood ratios neighbouring clusters.

title: IPTW identification weights — .iptw_weights
text: Cluster-level inverse-probability weights (Leung 2025; Proposition 3.9(iv)): $$\beta_{ij}(\phi_1) = 1\{C_{N_{ij}} = 1\} / P(C_{N_{ij}} = 1), \quad       \beta_{ij}(\phi_0) = 1\{C_{N_{ij}} = 0\} / P(C_{N_{ij}} = 0),$$ probabilities use cluster-level assignment law (distC, paramsC) \(k = |N^{cl}_{ij}|\) distinct neighbouring clusters. Units whose neighbouring clusters treated (phi_1) control (phi_0) get weight 0.

what: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
text: Computes Hajek LW point estimate \(\hat\mu = \sum_i u_i b_i Y_i / \sum_i u_i b_i\) one estimand per-unit centred contribution column \(V_i = u_i b_i (Y_i - \hat\mu)\).

title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand

title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
text: b per-unit identification weight column. Y observed outcomes. u per-unit weights.

title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
text: list point estimate mu, contribution column   V, flag ok (FALSE denominator 0   non-finite).

title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
text: NOTE: following definition \(\hat\Sigma^K\) Section 5 companion manuscript, contribution divided Hajek denominator \(D = \sum_i u_i b_i\) (converges 1; see estimator definition Section 4). point estimate properly normalised Hajek ratio. finite-sample denominator D departs noticeably 1, dividing V D yields sharper variance.

title: Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column — .lw_estimand
code: set.seed(1) Y <- rnorm(10); b <- runif(10); u <- rep(1 / 10, 10) est <- generalClusterExp:::.lw_estimand(b, Y, u) est$mu               # Hajek ratio sum(u * b * Y) / sum(u * b) #> [1] -0.1037307 sum(est$V)           # centred contributions sum to 0 #> [1] -6.938894e-18

title: Marginal Radon–Nikodym (MRN) identification weights — .marg_rn_weights
text: Per-unit marginal Radon–Nikodym weights \(\alpha_{ij}(\phi_c)\) (Theorem 3.6, Proposition 3.9()) two counterfactual regimes. weights marginalise within-cluster assignment neighbouring cluster, unit contributes whenever cluster neighbourhood positive probability regimes.

text: n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix (self-loops). C integer vector cluster ids. Y numeric vector observed outcomes. W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments. W_Y 0/1 vector individual-level treatments. weights1, weights0 per-regime identification weights (one weight constructors). p1_own, p0_own per-unit -treatment probabilities phi_1 phi_0. unit_weights optional per-unit weights (default: uniform). method "mrn", "iptw" "crn". design "bernoulli" "complete".

title: Estimation engine: weights to tidy output — .run_engine
code: set.seed(1) A <- Matrix::Matrix(outer(1:12, 1:12, function(i, j) abs(i - j) <= 1) * 1,                     sparse = TRUE) C <- rep(1:3, each = 4); W_C <- c(1, 0, 1) W_Y <- rbinom(12, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2)) Y <- rnorm(12, mean = 2 * as.vector(A %*% W_Y)) w <- generalClusterExp:::.iptw_weights(A, C, W_C,                                        distC = "binom",                                        paramsC = list(prob = 0.7)) out <- generalClusterExp:::.run_engine(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,   weights1 = w$weights1, weights0 = w$weights0,   p1_own = rep(0.5, 12), p0_own = rep(0.2, 12),   unit_weights = NULL, method = "iptw", design = "bernoulli") out$causal_effects #>                       effect            key  estimate     variance           se #> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall -2.103593 1.714485e-01 4.140634e-01 #> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1  3.354088 6.939894e-02 2.634368e-01 #> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0        NA           NA           NA #> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1  0.691480 4.683862e-31 6.843874e-16 #> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0        NA           NA           NA #> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total        NA           NA           NA #>   well_defined #> 1         TRUE #> 2         TRUE #> 3        FALSE #> 4         TRUE #> 5        FALSE #> 6        FALSE

title: IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights) — iptw
text: Linear-weighted Hajek estimator using cluster-level IPTW identification weights Leung (2025) (Proposition 3.9(iv)). outputs variance rule mrn: \(\hat\Sigma_1\) (Theorem 5.4) Bernoulli randomization bias-corrected \(\hat\Sigma_3\) (Theorem 5.11(ii)) complete randomization.

title: IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights) — iptw
code: iptw(   A,   C,   Y,   W_C,   W_Y,   dist1 = "binom",   params1 = list(prob = 0.5),   dist0 = "binom",   params0 = list(prob = 0),   distC = "binom",   paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),   unit_weights = NULL,   design = NULL )

title: IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights) — iptw
text: n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix interference network (self-loops, used throughout project). C integer vector length n_unit giving unit's cluster id. Y numeric vector observed outcomes (length n_unit). W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments, indexed cluster id. W_Y 0/1 vector individual-level treatments (length n_unit). dist1, params1 within-cluster assignment law treated regime phi_1. dist0, params0 within-cluster assignment law control regime phi_0. distC, paramsC cluster-level assignment law. unit_weights optional per-unit weights u_i = g_i / N_i (default: uniform 1 / n_unit). design optional override, "bernoulli" "complete"; inferred distC NULL.

title: IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights) — iptw
text: See mrn.

title: IPTW estimator (inverse-probability-of-treatment weights) — iptw
code: ## Same data-generating pipeline as in the mrn() example: geometric ## cluster network, two-stage Bernoulli treatment, interference outcomes. set.seed(1) n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per) centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4 loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2) A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1  W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7) W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2)) Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +                  W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))  ## IPTW keeps only units whose neighbouring clusters are all treated ## (for phi_1) or all control (for phi_0), reweighting by the inverse ## exposure probability. fit <- iptw(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,             params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),             distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7)) fit$variance_type #> [1] "var_1 (Loewner-max, Bernoulli)" fit$causal_effects #>                       effect            key estimate   variance        se #> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 7.923015 1.76868306 1.3299184 #> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 4.366624 2.33906215 1.5293993 #> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 2.251229 0.02132106 0.1460173 #> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 7.496872 2.90504985 1.7044207 #> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 5.381477 0.29326263 0.5415373 #> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 9.748101 2.92637091 1.7106639 #>   well_defined #> 1         TRUE #> 2         TRUE #> 3         TRUE #> 4         TRUE #> 5         TRUE #> 6         TRUE

title: MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights) — mrn
text: Linear-weighted Hajek estimator using marginal Radon–Nikodym identification weights (Theorem 3.6, Proposition 3.9()). Returns well-defined causal effects population average potential outcomes variance estimates. variance estimator Loewner-max HAC estimator \(\hat\Sigma_1\) (Theorem 5.4) cluster-level Bernoulli randomization, bias-corrected estimator \(\hat\Sigma_3 = \hat\Sigma_1 - \hat M\) (Theorem 5.11(ii)) cluster-level complete randomization.

title: MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights) — mrn
code: mrn(   A,   C,   Y,   W_C,   W_Y,   dist1 = "binom",   params1 = list(prob = 0.5),   dist0 = "binom",   params0 = list(prob = 0),   distC = "binom",   paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),   unit_weights = NULL,   design = NULL )

title: MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights) — mrn
text: n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix interference network (self-loops, used throughout project). C integer vector length n_unit giving unit's cluster id. Y numeric vector observed outcomes (length n_unit). W_C 0/1 vector cluster-level treatments, indexed cluster id. W_Y 0/1 vector individual-level treatments (length n_unit). dist1, params1 within-cluster assignment law treated regime phi_1. dist0, params0 within-cluster assignment law control regime phi_0. distC, paramsC cluster-level assignment law. unit_weights optional per-unit weights u_i = g_i / N_i (default: uniform 1 / n_unit). design optional override, "bernoulli" "complete"; inferred distC NULL.

title: MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights) — mrn
text: list causal_effects, potential_outcomes (data   frames estimates / variances / standard errors), estimand covariance   matrix Sigma, chosen variance_type.

title: MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights) — mrn
code: ## Small geometric cluster network (a scaled-down version of the ## simulation pipeline in data_generation.R): units live around ten ## cluster centres and interfere with all units within distance 1.5. set.seed(1) n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per)                      # cluster ids centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4   # cluster centres loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2) # unit locations A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1  ## Two-stage assignment: clusters are treated w.p. 0.7 (cluster-level ## Bernoulli law distC); units in treated clusters get W = 1 w.p. 0.5 ## (regime phi_1), units in control clusters w.p. 0.2 (regime phi_0). W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7) W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))  ## Outcomes with neighbourhood interference (spillover beta = 2 from ## treated neighbours plus interaction gamma = 1 for treated units). Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +                  W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))  ## MRN estimator under cluster-level Bernoulli randomization: ## variance is the Loewner-max HAC estimator Sigma1 (Theorem 5.4). fit <- mrn(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,            dist1 = "binom", params1 = list(prob = 0.5),            dist0 = "binom", params0 = list(prob = 0.2),            distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7)) fit$variance_type #> [1] "var_1 (Loewner-max, Bernoulli)" fit$causal_effects #>                       effect            key estimate  variance        se #> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 5.959401 2.1183410 1.4554521 #> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 5.066717 2.1529917 1.4673076 #> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 4.850573 0.5533077 0.7438466 #> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 4.111063 2.1116946 1.4531671 #> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 3.894918 0.3836304 0.6193790 #> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 8.961636 2.9628774 1.7213011 #>   well_defined #> 1         TRUE #> 2         TRUE #> 3         TRUE #> 4         TRUE #> 5         TRUE #> 6         TRUE fit$potential_outcomes #>       estimand          key estimate  variance        se well_defined #> 1   Ybar(phi1)    Ybar_phi1 7.207591 1.6561191 1.2869029         TRUE #> 2   Ybar(phi0)    Ybar_phi0 1.248190 0.6661849 0.8162015         TRUE #> 3 Ybar(1,phi1) Ybar_w1_phi1 9.180187 2.3992024 1.5489359         TRUE #> 4 Ybar(0,phi1) Ybar_w0_phi1 4.113469 0.4024912 0.6344219         TRUE #> 5 Ybar(1,phi0) Ybar_w1_phi0 5.069124 0.4852292 0.6965840         TRUE #> 6 Ybar(0,phi0) Ybar_w0_phi0 0.218551 0.3056427 0.5528496         TRUE  ## Cluster-level complete randomization (exactly 7 of 10 clusters ## treated, distC = "hypergeom"): the bias-corrected variance ## estimator Sigma3 of Theorem 5.11(ii) is used automatically. W_C2 <- as.integer(seq_len(K) %in% sample.int(K, 7)) W_Y2 <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C2[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2)) Y2 <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y2) +                   W_Y2 * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y2)) + rnorm(n)) fit_bc <- mrn(A, C, Y2, W_C2, W_Y2,               params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),               distC = "hypergeom", paramsC = list(m = 7)) fit_bc$variance_type #> [1] "var_1 bias-corrected (complete rand.)" fit_bc$causal_effects #>                       effect            key estimate  variance        se #> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 2.997105 0.5362698 0.7323044 #> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 4.383455 0.1773443 0.4211227 #> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 2.806703 0.5536457 0.7440737 #> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 3.297785 0.6898760 0.8305878 #> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 1.721033 0.2962016 0.5442440 #> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 6.104488 0.6063437 0.7786807 #>   well_defined #> 1         TRUE #> 2         TRUE #> 3         TRUE #> 4         TRUE #> 5         TRUE #> 6         TRUE
